flawed_step: Line 0218 incorrectly replaces the rightmost F(f,id_D) from naturality with G(f,id_D); line 0236 then relies on the corrected, unproved version while citing (3).
counterexample: Let C have objects 0,1 and one nonidentity arrow f:0→1; let D be terminal and E=Set. Define F(0,*)=G(0,*)={x}, F(1,*)=G(1,*)={0,1}, with F(f,id)(x)=0 and G(f,id)(x)=1. Let α_(0,*) be the identity and let α_(1,*) swap 0 and 1. The fixed-D slice is natural because G(f,id)α_(0,*)(x)=1=α_(1,*)F(f,id)(x), and fixed-C naturality over terminal D is automatic. But line 0218 claims G(f,id)α_(0,*)=α_(1,*)G(f,id); evaluated at x, the left side is 1 while the right side is α_(1,*)(1)=0.
assessment_summary: The sufficient-condition proof contains a false equation at line 0218 and later cites it to justify a different equation. The explicit finite-set example satisfies both stated slice-naturality assumptions but refutes the displayed claim.
